preModelEnvironmentFailure.class: pre-model environment failure (public.ecr.aws anonymous pull throttle, HTTP 429 "Data limit exceeded")
preModelEnvironmentFailure.whyNotTheModelOrTheCandidate: Nothing ran in any of the three attempts: no provider call, no tool call, no container, no attempt evidence, no usage. The failure is the GitHub-hosted runner's Docker client being refused by public.ecr.aws while building the task image, which is the host environment the task container is created in.
preModelEnvironmentFailure.whyOneMoreAttemptIsNotRepetition: The refusal is a shared anonymous-pull quota keyed to the runner's egress IP, and this batch measured that directly: of three seed jobs that pulled from the same repository in the same dispatch (run 39189195640), exactly one was refused with the same 429 while two succeeded. Repeating the pull is therefore a lottery over runner IPs — three losses in a row is what the cell has already drawn. This attempt removes the quota dependency instead of drawing again.

mitigation.declaredCompositionDelta: The image is delivered from a digest-pinned GHCR mirror instead of the read-only public registry that refused it. Nothing else changes: the corpus pin, the task sources, the harness, the task's Dockerfile, the candidate pin (02117de8c / 0.0.11-beta.1), the provider (glm-5.3 at reasoning effort high through dim-oauth), fh_agent_timeout_multiplier=1, the cell's 5400 s official budget and the per-call ceiling (1,800,000 ms) are exactly what the source run declared. The task source and the Dockerfile keep their pinned bytes because the mirror is aliased to the pinned reference locally, so no source file is rewritten and the frozen per-task record's task.dockerImage stays the reference the Dockerfile actually uses.

proofRun.job: Prove the offline local-alias build (same run 39189195640)
proofRun.howItProvesIt: On a fresh runner with no local image: the source registry host was blackholed in /etc/hosts (127.0.0.1 public.ecr.aws and 127.0.0.1 registry-1.public.ecr.aws), the digest-pinned mirror was pulled from GHCR, aliased to the pinned reference, and a docker compose build was run with a Dockerfile whose only image line is `FROM public.ecr.aws/d3j8x8q7/swe-bench-202605:kh7fkjmy67qny9z98mt6bj52m182ygdy-v1.1` plus pier's own `pull_policy: build`; the build completed and executed its RUN step (`#6 [2/2] RUN echo alias-resolved-from-local`, `#7 naming to docker.io/library/alias-probe-main done`), which is only possible if the pinned reference resolved from the local alias rather than from the registry.

mitigation.inJobGuard: The Generate job re-proves the same thing in the very job that runs the attempt, immediately before the harness: it pulls the mirror, aliases it, blackholes the source registry, and refuses to continue unless the probe build passes; it then restores /etc/hosts and writes results/candidate/image-mirror-receipt.json, which travels in this run's own artifacts. A plumbing failure therefore fails the job before the harness runs and can never consume the attempt.
mitigation.whyMirrorRatherThanAuthenticatedPull: The user offered either. An authenticated pull from public.ecr.aws needs an AWS principal (ecr-public:GetAuthorizationToken plus long-lived access keys as new repository secrets in this public repository) and only shifts the quota to that account; the GHCR mirror needs no new external credential at all (it uses this repository's own GITHUB_TOKEN), and its identity is checkable by digest rather than by trusting the transport. The mirror is therefore the variant this manifest declares. Authenticated ECR pull remains available as a future alternative if the mirror is ever unavailable, and it is recorded here as not used.
mitigation.workflowDelta: One declared, inert-by-default change to .github/workflows/frontier-harness.yml (commit e5e19ae): the optional fh_image_mirror / fh_mirror_image / fh_mirror_repo inputs, the mirror and proof jobs (which run only when fh_mirror_image is set), packages: read, and the consumer step in the Generate job (which runs only when fh_image_mirror is set). Every run that leaves both inputs empty is bit-for-bit the workflow the source run used: ruby YAML parse plus bash -n over all 25 embedded scripts, and npm test (256 tests, 0 failures), were run on this change before it was committed.
mitigation.notAConditionThatMakesTheCellPassable: The change touches only how the frozen image bytes reach the runner. It does not alter the image contents (digest-identical), the task instruction, the workspace, the tool surface, the model, the effort, the budgets or the grader, so it cannot make the task easier or the verdict gentler; the cell still has to be solved by the model inside the same container the source run declared.
